brief: September's US jobs report came in soft: non-farm payrolls rose just 29,000 against a 90,000 consensus, and the unemployment rate rose to 4.18% from 4.14% despite immigration enforcement shrinking the labor pool. Annual payroll growth held at 0.2% yoy, the household survey showed a 0.3% yoy employment decline, and hourly earnings growth cooled to 3.0% yoy, below August's 3.4% CPI. Berenberg argues this weak hiring undercuts the case for a fresh global tightening cycle, and investors responded by paring back rate-hike bets and reversing part of this week's Treasury yield rise. The bank doubts the Fed will tighten as much as the roughly three more 25bp hikes the market prices in and expects just one, with a pause signalled by central banks early next year letting yields ease slightly, though that respite should prove temporary as slower growth raises debt-sustainability questions. Separately, Berenberg still expects solid Q3 growth from consumer spending, but flags fragility: rising fuel prices, cooling confidence, a widening trade deficit (on course for 4.6% of GDP in Q3) showing AI infrastructure spending leaking into Asian imports, and a view that AI investment won't offset a consumer slowdown if household budgets buckle.
